column1: # Curated catalog of well-characterized human variants for trait/pharmacogenomic lookup.
# PUBLIC REFERENCE DATA ONLY — this file contains no individual's genotype.
# Coordinates are GRCh38. They are display/fallback only: 06_trait_report.sh
# resolves each variant by rsID against your own VCF, which is authoritative,
# and flags any REF/ALT mismatch against this table.
# All "effect_allele" values are the ALT (derived) allele on the forward strand,
# so a homozygous-reference genotype always means zero copies of the effect allele.
# Single-variant associations are simplifications. Effects describe statistical
# associations in studied populations, NOT deterministic outcomes or diagnoses.

column10: effect
With rs7412 defines APOE haplotype; C here marks the ε4 allele (higher Alzheimer's & LDL risk)
T marks the protective ε2 allele; interpret jointly with rs429358
A (677T) lowers MTHFR enzyme activity; may raise homocysteine, higher folate need
G (1298C) mildly reduces MTHFR activity, especially combined with 677T
A (ALDH2*2) causes acetaldehyde build-up: facial flushing, low alcohol tolerance
A allele keeps lactase switched on into adulthood (can digest milk); GG = likely lactose intolerant
AA (*1F/*1F) = fast caffeine metabolizer; C carriers clear caffeine more slowly
T (577X) removes alpha-actinin-3; TT skews toward endurance, CC toward power/sprint
G = H63D; milder iron-overload allele, risk mainly when combined with C282Y
A = C282Y; main hemochromatosis risk allele, esp. homozygous or with H63D
A allele associated with modestly higher BMI and appetite
G (118G) alters mu-opioid receptor; linked to differing opioid/analgesia response
GG associated in some studies with higher empathy/prosociality (weak, debated)
A (Met) = slower COMT, more prefrontal dopamine ("worrier"); G (Val) = "warrior"
A allele associated with heavier smoking and higher nicotine dependence
GG strongly associated with blue eyes; AA with brown
A (Ala111Thr) = lighter skin; near-fixed in European ancestry
TT = dry earwax and reduced body odor (common in East Asian ancestry)
C (Pro49) = taster of bitter PTC/PROP; GG = non-taster
A (A1) associated with lower D2 receptor density; studied in reward/addiction
T allele = greater warfarin sensitivity; lower dose typically needed
A (*2) = loss of function; reduced clopidogrel activation (poor metabolizer)
T (*2) = reduced CYP2C9 activity; slower metabolism of warfarin and some NSAIDs
C (*3) = strongly reduced CYP2C9 activity; lower drug-clearance
CC = Duffy-null: benign lower neutrophil counts and P. vivax malaria resistance
